memos.headline: S08 and S09 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S02 and S07 Breaking Down
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market today. S08 and S09 are the standout leaders: both sit within 3% of their 52-week highs, well above their 50- and 200-day means, with RSIs in the low 60s and dominant relative strength versus SPY (+10.6% and +6.4% over 4 weeks, respectively). S04 has strong 12-week momentum (+25.8%) but is extended at +9.2% above its 50-day mean and has pulled back nearly 3% this week, so I'd wait for a consolidation before adding. On the weak side, S02 is flashing oversold signals with an RSI of 35.5, a -13.1% drawdown, and negative relative strength on both 4- and 12-week horizons—this is a broken trend, not a buying opportunity until it reclaims its 50-day mean (~$409). S07 is the worst relative performer in the universe at -15.3% vs SPY over 12 weeks and sits 23% off its high; I'd avoid until it can hold above its 200-day mean area (~$778).

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: +29.1% over 26w, only -2.3% from highs, RSI 62.8, and leading SPY by +10.6% over 4w; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~$318).
Clean uptrend with +17% over 12w, +7% above 50d mean, RSI 61.6, and +15.1% relative strength vs SPY over 12w; invalidated below ~$155 (50d mean area).

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 and S01 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 is the standout: revenue doubled YoY to $96.22B with a 62.0% net margin and net income up 125.9%, all on modest $33.37B debt — this is durable, high-quality earnings growth. S05 printed a remarkable 93.7% net margin on $119.80B revenue with net income up nearly 298% YoY and only $14.79B in debt, though I want to understand the sustainability of that margin level before sizing up further. On the other end, S09 posted just 4.9% net margin with net income down 45.8% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth and $33.13B in debt — classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. S01 also concerns me: revenue grew only 1.5% YoY while net income fell 15.8%, and the $29.30B debt load relative to $3.04B in earnings leaves little room for error. I would change my view on S09 and S01 if subsequent quarters show margin stabilization and a return to positive earnings growth.

views.note: Revenue +105.9% YoY, 62.0% net margin, and $33.37B debt make this the best earnings-power profile in the universe.
Net income up 297.9% YoY with a 93.7% net margin and minimal $14.79B debt is extraordinary, though margin sustainability needs monitoring.
39.7% net margin on $90.01B revenue with 17.7% YoY growth and manageable $40.29B debt reflects durable, high-quality earnings.
Revenue of $200.61B (+19.6% YoY) and net income up 244.9% show powerful operating leverage, though $133B debt warrants attention.
Revenue +24.0% and net income +64.9% YoY with a 17.5% net margin show solid momentum, but $36.21B debt on $20.54B revenue is elevated.
Strong 36.9% margin and 27.7% revenue growth are offset by $460.52B in total debt, which dominates the balance sheet.
Solid 16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin, but $82.30B debt and decelerating growth versus peers keep me at neutral.
Revenue essentially flat at +0.4% YoY with a thin 4.9% margin; the 61% net income bounce helps but doesn't signal durable improvement yet.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on barely growing revenue — textbook cash-flow compression.
Revenue growth of just 1.5% with net income declining 15.8% and $29.30B debt versus $3.04B earnings signals deteriorating fundamentals.

memos.headline: Fed Paused but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Surging 10y Yields Signal a Hawkish-Hold Regime — Favor Banks and Staples, Avoid Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for three months, having cut 75bp over the prior year, but headline CPI is running at 3.3% YoY — well above target — which likely freezes any further easing. The labor market is firm with unemployment at 4.10%, down 20bp over both three and twelve months, removing any urgency to cut. The 10y yield at 4.96% has surged 95bp over the past year and 51bp in just three months, flattening the 10y-2y spread to 39bp; this repricing of term premium punishes long-duration assets and signals the bond market is pricing persistent inflation or fiscal risk. I have conviction that the pause extends into year-end and that the next move is more likely a hike than a cut if CPI prints above 3.5%. A materially weaker payroll or unemployment above 4.4% would flip my regime call toward renewed easing.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face headwinds from the 95bp YoY surge in 10y yields and no prospect of near-term rate cuts.
Banks benefit from a steep-enough curve (39bp 10y-2y), firm loan demand in a 4.1% unemployment economy, and elevated short rates supporting NIM.
Staples offer defensive positioning as sticky inflation and rising long yields compress multiples on growth; their pricing power supports margins at 3.3% CPI.
Cyclicals face mixed signals — solid employment supports demand but rising yields and a flattening curve hint at slowing momentum ahead.
Energy tends to hold up in inflationary pauses; 3.3% CPI and a firm labor market support commodity demand while rising yields don't compress energy multiples as much as growth.
High-duration growth names are most vulnerable to the 51bp three-month jump in 10y yields with no easing catalyst on the horizon.
Uncertain sector exposure; the macro backdrop of paused rates and rising long yields warrants a wait-and-see stance until the next CPI print clarifies direction.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S03, S04, S10 Positive Momentum vs. S08, S05 Negative Overhang
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in post-earnings sentiment across the universe. S03 (+15.3%), S04 (+15.5%), and S10 (+8.7%) all printed strongly positive price reactions to their results filings, suggesting narrative momentum that may still have legs—especially S10, whose earnings beat is the most recent (Aug 26) and was followed by a new material agreement and an Other Events 8-K, signaling continued corporate activity. On the negative side, S08 (-7.4%) and S05 (-7.1%) both saw sharp post-earnings declines in late July; S08's subsequent director departure/appointment amendment on Sep 1 adds management uncertainty that could keep tone depressed. S01's muted -1.9% reaction and triple 8-K filing cluster on Jul 29 (including officer changes and Reg FD) reads as noisy rather than directional, so I stay neutral there. I have lower conviction on names like S06 and S02 where we lack earnings price reactions and the filings are governance or Reg FD in nature—insufficient to form a sentiment view.

views.note: Massive +15.3% earnings reaction in late July and recent officer appointment suggest positive narrative momentum still building.
Strongest earnings pop in the universe at +15.5%; Sep 2 Reg FD filing keeps the company in the news without negative catalysts.
Most recent earnings beat (+8.7% on Aug 26) plus new debt agreement and follow-on Other Events 8-K suggest active positive corporate narrative.
Solid +5.6% earnings reaction and a new material definitive agreement on Sep 1 point to constructive tone, though magnitude is more modest.
Sharp -7.4% earnings selloff compounded by a director change 8-K/A on Sep 1 signals management instability and lingering negative sentiment.
Post-earnings drop of -7.1% in late July with only a generic Other Events filing since; no evidence of tone recovery.
Mild -1.9% earnings reaction and a cluster of three 8-Ks on the same day create noise rather than a clear directional signal.
No earnings price reaction available; bylaws amendment and Other Events filings are governance housekeeping with no sentiment signal.
Only a single Reg FD filing on Sep 8 with no earnings reaction data—insufficient to form a directional sentiment view.

memos.headline: Surging Policy Uncertainty and $103 Oil Signal Geopolitical Stress; Favor Energy Exposure, Caution on Policy-Sensitive Names
memos.body: I am flagging a sharp deterioration in the geopolitical-policy backdrop: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has surged 62.6% over one month and 150.5% over three months to 466.83, a level historically associated with major sanctions episodes or trade-war escalations. Simultaneously, WTI crude has jumped 23.7% in a month to $103.57/bbl, consistent with either supply disruption (sanctions enforcement, OPEC+ action, or conflict-related risk premium) or demand-side policy shock. Notably, credit spreads remain benign at 2.70% OAS and the VIX at 17.84 is actually down over three months, suggesting markets are not yet pricing a full-blown crisis—this divergence between policy uncertainty and market vol is where I see the most risk. Without granular detail on the 8-K filings beyond item codes, I cannot attribute company-specific policy exposure with high confidence, but the macro picture strongly favors energy-levered names and argues for caution on firms with heavy China/export-control sensitivity. A reversal in my view would require EPU falling below 300 or WTI retreating below $90, signaling de-escalation.

views.note: Two 8-Ks in quick succession (Aug-17, Sep-3) suggest active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot determine geopolitical exposure direction.
Recent Reg FD filing on Sep-8 amid peak policy uncertainty warrants monitoring but insufficient detail to take a directional stance.
Reg FD disclosure filed Sep-2 coincides with the sharpest phase of the EPU spike; if S04 has supply-chain or export-control exposure, the policy environment is hostile.
Dual Reg FD filings on the same July date suggest a material disclosure event, but the subsequent macro deterioration makes me cautious without more detail.
8.01 Other Events filing in August is too opaque to act on; elevated oil and policy uncertainty create a mixed backdrop.
If S06 has energy or commodity exposure, the $103 WTI environment and supply-side tightness are structurally supportive; July 8-K predates the worst of the uncertainty spike.
Early-August Reg FD filing with no content detail; the benign credit spread environment is a partial offset to elevated policy risk.
